**Plan:**

The blocking dependence is intra-iteration: line 6 writes to `u[ju[i]]` and line 7 reads from `u[ku[i]]` in the same iteration i. This sequential read-after-write within each iteration forces the loop to be sequential, even if there are no inter-iteration conflicts.

Solution: Split the loop into two separate loops. The first loop performs all u-updates; the second loop then performs all v-updates using the updated u values. This removes the intra-iteration dependence chain. Each resulting loop becomes independently parallelizable as a reduction pattern (where multiple iterations accumulate into the same array locations via the `+=` operator).

Output preservation: Because addition is commutative and associative, performing all line-6 operations in any order, then all line-7 operations in any order, gives the same result as the original sequential execution.Done. The loop has been split into two separate loops, removing the intra-iteration dependence chain. DiscoPoP should now detect a reduction pattern (or do-all, depending on the actual index patterns) in each of the two resulting loops, allowing pragmas to be inserted for parallel execution.
